comment: Codex over ACP. Separate from the `codex` adapter deliberately: this is a trial transport for an agent that already works over tmux, and merging them would put a working production agent behind an untested code path. Retire one of the two once a winner is clear.
notLaunchableReason: hafleet-up creates a tmux session and an ACP agent has no pane; start it with `hafleet acp-up <name> <workspace> codex-acp` instead

launch.permissionSummary: codex-acp asks before each tool call and hafleet declines all but its own coordination tools; hafleet passes NO filesystem sandbox flag on this transport
launch.commandNote: codex-acp is an adapter, not codex itself: it wraps the Codex SDK and speaks ACP on stdio. Unlike octos and hermes, whose vendors ship ACP directly, this puts a third-party process in the chain, version-coupled to both the adapter and the codex CLI underneath it. Installed from @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp; the older @zed-industries/codex-acp is deprecated in favour of it.
launch.permissionSummaryNote: It said "level2 (workspace-write + on-request)" — copied from codex.json — and half of that was false. The tmux transport really does pass --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request (bin/hafleet-up); this transport passes defaultArgs and acpArgs, both empty, so NO filesystem sandbox flag reaches the process. The approval half is real by a different mechanism: codex-acp asks the client via session/request_permission and hafleet answers allow_once only for its own coordination tools, declining everything else (see permissionNote, and lib/codex-permission-hook.js). So the summary now describes the mechanism that exists rather than naming a Codex level whose sandbox half nothing establishes — the same honesty octos.json already practises. This string is operator-facing (served by /api/frameworks, shown on the onboard page), and it is pinned in tests/fixtures/launch-policy-baseline.json so changing it stays a deliberate act. Giving the ACP transport a real filesystem sandbox is a separate, open decision: it needs verification that codex-acp accepts --sandbox and that the flag means the same thing over ACP as over a pane.
launch.acpModelFlagNote: codex-acp accepts --model without complaint and then ignores it — verified: the handshake succeeds either way. Declaring null so hafleet refuses the flag up front rather than letting an operator believe a model was selected when it was not.

acp.mcpServersNote: Verified live: codex-acp spawns the MCP server passed in session/new (observed as mcp-server.js with the vendored codex binary as its parent) and calls its tools. Unlike octos, which accepted the field and spawned nothing. Note it declares mcpCapabilities {acp:false, http:true, sse:false} — that governs MCP over the ACP connection itself, not the plain stdio server used here.
acp.declaredCapabilities: Verified live against codex-acp 1.1.9: protocolVersion 1, loadSession true, sessionCapabilities{resume,list,close,delete,additionalDirectories}, promptCapabilities{embeddedContext,image}, authMethods[api-key,chat-gpt]. session/new succeeded using the codex CLI's existing login, so this adapter carries no separate credential.
acp.permissionNote: codex-acp asks the CLIENT before running an MCP tool: session/request_permission with _meta.is_mcp_tool_approval, offering allow_once/allow_session/allow_always/decline. The request identifies the call only by toolCallId and carries no tool name, so the preceding tool_call update must be correlated to answer it. HAFleet answers allow_once for its own coordination tools and declines everything else, reusing lib/codex-permission-hook.js. octos never asks, which is why this gap went unnoticed until codex-acp hung every turn for the full 600s prompt timeout.
acp.verifiedEndToEnd: 2026-08-03: received a type=request over ACP, called check_inbox through HAFleet's MCP server, and replied via send_message (msg_0099, msg_0100, both 'PARITY'). Same contract as octos and the tmux agents.

flags.comment: Sandbox and approval level are chosen by HAFleet. The patterns cover the clustered short forms (-sfoo, -a=never) that a plain prefix match would miss.
flags.message: Codex Level 2 policy flag is managed by hafleet: {token}

config.comment: The same policy can be set through -c/--config, in four spellings: as a separate argument, and inline as --config=K=V, -c=K=V or -cK=V.
config.message: Codex Level 2 config is managed by hafleet: {key}
config.inlineMessage: Codex Level 2 config is managed by hafleet
